Microneedling — Internal Draft

A safe page structure is ready for clinical review. Active offering, provider, qualifications, candidacy, recovery, claims, and approved media remain unresolved.

Authentic media requiredPractice-owned microneedling room or device image

Use only approved equipment or treatment-room media. Do not represent stock or AI-generated people as the practice or as real outcomes.

Suggested slot: 1600×1200 desktop source; 800×600 mobile crop.

Clinical source gate

What this page must establish

Confirm the exact procedure, device, provider, skin-related indications, candidacy, contraindications, comfort, recovery variability, limitations, alternatives, and care instructions. Universal skin-type or outcome claims are not allowed without review.

Candidacy pendingRecovery pendingMedia pending

Page sections

Ready for exact clinical copy

Concerns addressed

Validate any discussion of texture, scarring, pores, lines, or tone against confirmed indications.

Provider & qualifications

Blocked until the performing provider and publishable qualifications are documented.

Consultation & candidacy

Start with goals, history, screening, alternatives, and clinician review; do not imply that a page can determine candidacy.

Safety, recovery & limitations

State variable recovery and limitations only after review. Avoid “safe for all skin types,” fixed series, fixed timelines, or guaranteed results.

Care instructions

The prior PDF is quarantined pending clinical owner and review date.

FAQ structure

Questions to complete

Is this treatment appropriate for every skin type?

No universal statement is permitted. The clinician must define candidacy and risk language.

What recovery is typical?

Use only clinician-approved, treatment-specific recovery guidance and explain individual variability.

What are the alternatives?

List only confirmed options that the clinician approves for the patient's concern.

Consultation CTA blocked

Enable only after the practice confirms the offering, provider, CTA destination, disclosures, and care instructions.
